answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with staked reputation bonds: every identity must lock a deposit — its pearl — before it can transact, and the bond is slashed when peers prove fraud. Like onyx, the bond is hard to fake and costly to replace, so spawning a thousand sock puppets means locking a thousand deposits. Trust then flows through karst-like channels: only identities with a history of completed, attested work earn endorsements, so fresh fakes start with zero reach and must pay full price to climb.
